findings.passage: Indiana requires valid photo ID when voting in person.
findings.note: Voter-information page on her campaign site lists photo ID among steps for voting in Indiana. It states the current rule and gives no view on changing it.

findings.passage: Voter registration and education should be clear, accessible, and nonpartisan. Every Hoosier deserves to understand how to participate without confusion or barriers.
findings.note: Quote on her voter-information page about registration and voter education.

findings.passage: Hundreds of thousands of voter records in Indiana have been marked inactive or removed in recent years.
findings.note: States a fact about voter-roll removals as a reason voters should check their registration.

findings.passage: Your registration information — your address, your primary ballot history, your driver's license number — belongs to you. I will treat it that way.
findings.note: Issues page, under protecting election integrity and privacy. Speaks about privacy of voter registration data, including the driver's license number; does not mention ID rules at the polls.

findings.passage: The Secretary of State's office should never be used as a tool to advance a political agenda or to hand sensitive voter data to outside interests.
findings.note: Issues page, on not sharing sensitive voter data with outside interests.

findings.passage: In recent years, federal officials have increasingly sought to influence state election policy by weighing in on mail-in voting rules, early voting access, voter roll maintenance, identification requirements, and congressional district maps. Hoosiers are best positioned to serve Hoosiers. Indiana does not need election mandates driven by national party priorities rather than the practical realities of voters on the ground.
findings.note: Campaign blog post. Mentions identification requirements only in a list of areas where federal officials weigh in, and argues against federal election mandates on states.
subjects: federal role in state election rules

findings.passage: Publishing audit findings, reporting both successes and failures, and clearly communicating corrective actions would go a long way toward rebuilding trust.
findings.note: Campaign blog post on election audits and public trust.

findings.passage: Support mail-in ballots and early voting as standard options for every Hoosier,
findings.note: One item in her accessibility plan: supports mail-in ballots and early voting as standard options. It names no ID rule for them.

findings.passage: I would actually, we already know that it's a felony to vote if you're not an American citizen. There's already checks and balances in place. What Mr. Engling is trying to propose is that we have more burdensome rules and regulations for people who are legally allowed to vote, but they now have to prove if you're a divorced woman, if you have married, if you're adopted and you have to produce a birth certificate, it's an undue, burden for them. It's an additional cost that not everyone on this stage would have to do.
findings.note: Rebuttal in the Secretary of State debate, answering an opponent's call to verify citizenship of voters. She says non-citizen voting is already a felony and checks exist, and describes the proposal as extra document burden (birth certificates) on eligible voters. Date is the PBS page's publication date; text is the page's auto-generated transcript, with the speaker named by the moderator as Ms. Schillings.

findings.passage: Again, we have checks and balances already in place for what we're doing. And I do believe that those are effective. We have caught the individuals and they're very minimal. And I, I think that we're in good shape there.
findings.note: Her answer to a moderator question on whether a crackdown on non-citizen voting is needed (she was asked to go first). She says current checks are effective and cases found are few. Auto-generated transcript; date is the PBS page's publication date.

findings.passage: That has a lot of privacy concerns. For me, it has information about each voter, what primary ballots they may have pulled, their location, their driver's license number and part of their social security numbers in there too," she said. "So it's easy to triangulate that information, and it's easy to misuse that kind of data in a government entity type of way.
findings.note: Quoted by WFYI/WBOI. She is speaking about the incumbent's handing of Indiana's voter roll data to the federal government, and says it raises privacy concerns. The article also reports she said her platform includes protecting the integrity of elections.
